prerequisites: Mathematics I and II (or similar) of 1st year of Chemical Industrial Engineering, Industrial Electronic Engineering, Electrical Engineering and Mechanical Engineering degrees at UAL

learning_outcomes.text: Be able to solve mathematical problems that may arise in Engineering.
Be able to formulate and solve various problems using appropriate Numerical Methods.
Be able to model theoretical and applied engineering problems related to linear or non-linear optimization, with or without constraints.
Be able to use computer tools to solve both optimization problems and numerical methods application problems, especially the Matlab language.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Numerical Solution of Equations
Non-linear equations, root localization and polynomial equations
Bisection and Newton-Raphson methods. Other methods
Topic 2. Numerical Solution of Systems of Equations
Direct methods for linear systems. Matrix factorization: LU and Cholesky
Iterative methods for linear systems: Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel
Iterative methods for non-linear systems: Newton-Raphson
Topic 3. Numerical Solution of Initial Value Problems (IVPs) and Boundary Value Problems (BVPs) for Differential Equations
IVPs for differential equations and systems of differential equations
Numerical methods for IVPs: Euler and Runge-Kutta methods
Boundary Value Problem for a second-order ODE
Finite difference method for BVPs
Topic 4. Interpolation and Function Approximation
Classical polynomial interpolation problem. Lagrange and Newton interpolation
Interpolation with splines
Approximation. Least squares fitting
Topic 5. Numerical Integration
Simple and composite elementary quadrature formulas
Topic 6. Optimization (mathematical programming)
Introduction to optimization. Linear, non-linear and integer optimization problems, with and without constraints.
Solution techniques in linear optimization
Solution techniques in non-linear optimization

assessment_methods.method: Computer practices with MATLAB (tests, exercises, problems)
Problem solving on Optimization (reports, assignments, problems)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 60% from the written final exam (A1), 30% from computer practices with MATLAB (A2), and 10% from problem solving on Optimization (A3). A minimum score of 4 out of 10 points is required for the written final exam (A1), and a minimum final grade of 5 out of 10 points is required to pass the course. In the ordinary examination, A2 and A3 are evaluated continuously and cannot be retaken. In the unique final evaluation and extraordinary examination, A2 and A3 are assessed via an additional written exam alongside A1; however, students may keep their continuous assessment grades for A2 and A3 from the teaching period if desired. The use of Artificial Intelligence tools is prohibited in all assessment activities.
